The point is that providers can rapidly scale out to handle both flash crowds and anticipated increases in demand, and no single CDN has to provision all the resources itself. Whether the peering is ad-hoc or planned, there's fundamental research needed on the core problems: measuring and disseminating load information, doing request assignment and redirection, enabling content replication, and figuring out appropriate compensation among participants, all at a geographically distributed Internet scale. In a single CDN those issues are deeply interrelated and depend on each other. The main thrust here is handling them in a coordinated, cooperative way across many peered CDNs, while still satisfying the complex multi-dimensional constraints each individual provider has."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Let's start with triggers.
